earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only survey/wordlist items (Shaw 1981 'Doso'; Shaw 1986 'The Bosavi language family'); no grammar or phonology found online

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages for Doso (doso1239), Doso-Turumsa (doso1238) and Turumsa (turu1250), plus the local Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib dump
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: the complete Glottolog bibliography tagged [dol] is Shaw 1981 (ms wordlist), Shaw 1986 (overview/wordlist) and Ethnologue; no grammar, grammar sketch, phonology or dictionary exists for Doso or for Turumsa (Turumsa Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are also a wordlist or less).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch): 'Doso', 'Turumsa' and 'Soari River' pages (families > Papuan Gulf > Strickland and Soari Rivers > Soari River). Last modified 2024-06-25.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: 'Phonology [under construction] …' on the Doso page and 'Historical phonology [under construction]' on the Soari River page -- no content. Gives the source inventory (Spaulding/Shaw 1981: 107 terms, Kesigi; Shaw 1986: 73 terms; Carr 2002: Makapa; Rueck, MacKenzie & Alemán 2005: 8-20, 156 terms) and Doso pronouns after Carr 2002 with stress marks on the duals (1dl õu'pãɾe, 2dl nu'pãɾẽmẽ, 3dl 'usepãɾe); 'No information about Doso or Turumsa verbal morphology is available to us.' Wordlist-level marks only, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: documentation status only: 'Yet another language to the south is Doso, attested only in unpublished Summer Institute of Linguistics survey data and by a short wordlist taken from a second language speaker in Shaw (1986: 68).. Doso, however, is reported to have 61 % lexicostatistical similarity with the newly discovered and highly endangered Turumsa language, for which no data has yet been published (Tupper 2007c).' Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar and Timothy Usher. 2017. The Kamula-Elevala language family. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 35: 106-131. ISSN 0023-1959.
sources.note: For Doso: wordlist-only data -- ten Doso/Turumsa forms in phonetic brackets with primary-stress marks copied from Rueck, Alemán & MacKenzie 2005 ([a:] 'father', ['wai] 'mother', ['bapa] 'older brother', ['nana] 'older sister', ['omari] 'blood', [ka'pia] 'wallaby', [wa:taɾa] 'cassowary', ['waɾa] 'cloud', ['asiɾa] 'sand'; Turumsa [kù'ko] 'belly' with a grave-marked vowel), no statement about Doso stress or tone. The prosodic statements in the paper are about Kamula ('There are three tones: high, low, and rising (Routamaa and Routamaa 1995: 14).. Vowel length is conditioned by stress. Long phone…

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. hdl:10125/4478.
sources.note: no phonology content: documentation-status remark only (author had insufficient access to any Doso/Turumsa data; lexicostatistic percentages from Tupper 2007); the paper's criterion is whether a sketch grammar's worth of data exists, and Doso-Turumsa is listed among families where it does not.

sources.citation: Tupper, Ian. 2007. Endangered Languages Listing: TURUMSA [tqm]. 1 p. Document posted at pnglanguages.org (Glottolog ref 61402; socling).
sources.note: 1-page sociolinguistic listing for the sister language Turumsa; no phonology expected.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon. TransNewGuinea.org entry 'Doso' (73 lexical items, all from Shaw 1986)
sources.note: Lexical database only; sole source Shaw 1986; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel. 1986. The Bosavi language family. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24, 45-76. Pacific Linguistics A-70. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A70.45
sources.note: Nothing. The 'cursory phonological examination' (pp.47-49, Table 1) covers /p/~/f/ distribution, consonant and vowel inventories, and supra-segmentals limited to nasalisation, length, labialisation and open/closed syllables for the surveyed Bosavi-family languages; Doso is NOT in Table 1. Doso appears only in note 4 ('no complete wordlists are available') and as a partial wordlist in Appendix A, taken at Kisigi from a Kamula man married to a Doso woman. No stress/accent statement for any language, and none for Doso.

sources.citation: Wood, Michael. 1982. Kamula social structure and ritual. PhD dissertation, Macquarie University, Sydney. (cited by Shaw 1986 n.4 as the source on the Doso group)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Anthropological thesis on the neighbouring Kamula that Shaw cites for the existence and migration of the Doso; very unlikely to contain phonology but is the only other work Shaw names in connection with Doso.

sources.citation: Shaw, Daniel. 1981. Doso. Unpublished ms., 9 pp. (SIL-PNG survey wordlist; Glottolog ref 718134, file held by Glottolog editors, not shareable)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only Doso-specific document known to exist; a survey wordlist may carry phonetic stress marks or a one-line note on accent, though as a 9-page wordlist it probably has no prose phonology.
